context.exploration_scope: Reused PHASE-SSI-S5's operationally-validated Principle in a real SSI decision flow: computed an independent judgment first (no reference to the Principle), then a Principle-guided judgment, then compared them before deciding whether to let the Principle inform the real decision

problem: PHASE-SSI-S5 proved the Principle agrees with the independent convention on one test case, but the Principle had never actually been let anywhere near a real decision this automation would act on -- reusing it required first re-proving, on this real occasion, that it still is not the thing deciding whether it is trustworthy.

result.note: The Principle-guided judgment matched the independently-computed judgment on a real decision case -- the Principle was allowed to inform (corroborate, not override) the real decision, still with 0 CI/policy/execution wiring.

cause.root_cause_summary: Letting a Principle participate in a real decision without first computing an independent judgment blind to it would make any future agreement uninformative -- the independent judgment has to exist before the Principle is consulted, or "the Principle was right" and "the Principle was the only opinion asked" become indistinguishable.

lesson: Reusing a validated Principle in a real decision is safe only if the decision process still produces an independent answer on its own first -- the Principle is then evidence to compare against that answer, not a replacement for computing it, and a mismatch has to be able to actually block the Principle from being applied rather than being logged and overridden anyway.
